blanks.sentence: In the past, most birthday cakes were _____.
blanks.section: NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS — A change over time

blanks.sentence: Many present-day cakes are edible _____ rather than plain party food.
Her favourite fruit flavours for a cake are _____.
She values the cake's taste and _____ more than a tidy appearance.
Customers have seen his _____, which helps them trust him with a new commission.
He wants his finished cakes to be _____ to the people receiving them, even after the celebration.
To develop decoration ideas, he learns about each person's _____.

multipleChoice.question: What broader change in birthday cakes does the discussion describe?
options: Cakes have increasingly become edible designs that reflect the person celebrating.
Cakes have increasingly been chosen for the number of candles they can hold.
Cakes have increasingly followed one standard design for every celebration.
Cakes have increasingly been prepared at home for a more personal occasion.

multipleChoice.question: Why would an unevenly decorated cake still suit the first baker's ideal?
options: It could show that the cake was made without any planning.
It could take less time to make than a carefully flavoured cake.
It could still be fresh and taste the way she wants.
It could make the customer's hobbies easier to recognise.

multipleChoice.question: How are the two approaches to birthday cakes presented?
options: The first baker seeks impressive decoration; the newer baker values speed above appearance.
The first baker favours simple, flavourful cakes; the newer baker gives greater attention to visual design.
The first baker follows customers' hobbies; the newer baker prefers familiar fruit flavours.
The first baker creates cakes to be remembered; the newer baker focuses on making them at home.

multipleChoice.question: What makes designing cakes personally satisfying for the second baker?
options: It lets him repeat earlier designs for a wider range of customers.
It lets him avoid learning about the people receiving the cakes.
It lets him judge how long other bakers spend on each cake.
It gives him room to express himself through his work.

multipleChoice.question: A new client says, "I trust your ideas; you choose the design." Which response best fits the second baker's approach?
options: He develops his own ideas while keeping the client's satisfaction in mind.
He develops the cake without considering the recipient.
He assumes the client is no longer concerned with appearance.
He promises to reproduce a cake from his earlier designs.

multipleChoice.question: What does the baker enjoy about revealing the finished cake?
options: The reveal helps him decide whether to change the cake's flavour.
The reveal gives him a chance to see whether the customer is pleased.
The reveal is when his clients first grant him design freedom.
The reveal shows that every cake takes longer than clients expect.
